themes_detail.label: Street Lights Going Dark
themes_detail.summary: Street light outages in CD 208 spiked THIS WEEK to 19 complaints vs. a 9.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 95% increase (z-score: 4.99)—raising safety concerns as winter daylight hours shrink in a district with known traffic and pedestrian safety priorities.
evidence: 19 street light complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (95% spike, z-score 4.99)
Spike is statistically significant and the most recent anomaly in the dataset
Aligns with CB budget priorities requesting improved traffic and pedestrian safety (DOT agency)
reporting_angles: Map the dark zones: which Riverdale/Fieldston blocks are without lights and for how long?
Interview residents about safety fears during evening commutes and early darkness; get NYPD/DOE response times

themes_detail.label: Rodent Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped 220% LAST WEEK to 20 reports vs. a 6.2 weekly average (z-score: 5.04), marking the third consecutive spike signal and suggesting either a seasonal surge or a localized infestation cluster in Riverdale.
evidence: 20 rodent complaints LAST WEEK vs. 6.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (220% increase, z-score 5.04)
Third ranked spike in the dataset by recency after street lights and door/window issues
Statistically significant deviation suggests possible infestation hotspot rather than random variation
reporting_angles: Investigate whether complaints cluster geographically (e.g., one building, one block, near parks or waterfront)
Interview residents and local pest control vendors; get Health Dept. inspection data for the district
Ask: Is this seasonal (winter) or a sign of housing code violations / unsanitary conditions?

themes_detail.label: Smoking/Vaping Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about smoking and vaping in CD 208 surged 389% LAST WEEK to 11 reports vs. a 2.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.94), suggesting either increased enforcement awareness or a new behavioral trend in shared residential spaces.
evidence: 11 smoking/vaping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (389% spike, z-score 3.94)
Statistically significant anomaly ranked 7th in spike severity
Suggests either new community awareness campaign or concentrated violation pattern
reporting_angles: Who is filing complaints and where? (apartment buildings, parks, sidewalks?) Does it indicate tenant enforcement or new NYPD focus?
Interview building managers about secondhand smoke complaints and lease enforcement challenges

themes_detail.label: Tree and Root Damage Wave
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints exploded 3,100% TWO WEEKS AGO (4 reports vs. 0.1 baseline, z-score 11.72) and root/sewer/sidewalk damage spiked 1,500% (4 reports vs. 0.2 baseline, z-score 8.66), suggesting widespread infrastructure damage from recent weather or aging tree stock in a district seeking park upgrades.
evidence: Dead/dying trees: 4 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average (3,100% increase, z-score 11.72—highest in dataset)
Root/sewer/sidewalk damage: 4 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,500% increase, z-score 8.66—second highest)
Aligns with CB budget requests for park renovation and new equipment for maintenance (Parks Dept.)
reporting_angles: Were these triggered by recent weather (ice, wind, heavy rain)? Check NWS data from 2-3 weeks ago.
Map the damage: which parks, streets, and blocks are most affected? Interview Parks Dept. about response timeline.
Frame as evidence for CB's standing budget request for park and infrastructure upgrades

themes_detail.label: Door and Window Repair Backlog
themes_detail.summary: Door and window complaints rose 82% LAST WEEK to 23 reports vs. a 12.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.86), likely reflecting heating season demand and aging housing stock in a district with repeated requests for building maintenance resources.
evidence: 23 door/window complaints LAST WEEK vs. 12.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (82% increase, z-score 3.86)
Spike coincides with winter season when drafts, leaks, and heating loss become urgent
Suggests possible backlog in building maintenance or landlord response times
reporting_angles: Survey residents: how long are repair requests taking? Are landlords responding to complaints?
Cross-check with Heat/Hot Water complaints (1,675 in 90 days)—are these related to poor building envelope?
